description: Context profile for common problems, fixes, and patterns in the tradeBotServer codebase

gui_account_pnl_zero.problem: Master GUI account banner shows $0.00 unrealized/realized PnL even with open positions
symptoms: Account bar unrealized/realized stays at $0.00 during session
Positions widget shows non-zero PnL but banner stays zero
root_causes: TopStepX position payload often does not include unrealizedPnL fields
Account banner endpoint aggregated non-existent fields instead of computing PnL
Correct PnL computation existed in /api/chart/positions but banner didn't reuse it

solutions.fix: Compute unrealized PnL by summing per-position computed PnL from handle_get_positions() (which fetches quotes + uses tick/point values). Realized PnL from AccountTracker.get_state() when available.

prevention: Prefer computing PnL from entry price + current quote + tick/point values over trusting API fields
Reuse canonical formatting/normalization path (handle_get_positions) for consistent UI

strategy_signals_not_in_gui.problem: Strategy signals execute (orders placed) but Strategy Signals widget shows nothing
symptoms: Signal feed remains 'No signals yet...' while strategies log signals
No 'signal' WebSocket messages received by frontend
root_causes: Some strategies (e.g. SimpleCandleStrategy) run their own loop and bypass StrategyManager._run_strategy broadcast path
Signals were only broadcast from StrategyManager._run_strategy, not from self-loop strategies

solutions.fix: Add StrategyManager.broadcast_signal() helper that broadcasts to GUI via gui.chart_html.broadcast_update and sends Discord signal notification.
Call trading_bot.strategy_manager.broadcast_signal(...) when a signal is detected in the strategy's own loop.

prevention: Any strategy that runs its own loop must call a common broadcast helper when signals are generated
Keep all signal broadcasting in one helper to avoid drift between strategies

strategy_orders_no_discord.problem: Strategy-initiated orders do not trigger Discord order notifications
symptoms: Signals appear in logs but no Discord order notifications
Manual CLI orders notify but strategy orders do not
root_causes: Strategy order placement did not pass strategy_name down to adapter/order executor
Rust hot path didn't send strategy-order notifications even when Python fallback did

solutions.fix: Pass strategy_name=self.config.name into trading_bot.place_oco_bracket_with_stop_entry so adapter can attribute strategy orders.
Send Discord order notification on Rust hot path when strategy_name is provided.
Set adapter back-reference self.broker_adapter._trading_bot = self so adapter can access DiscordNotifier.

prevention: Ensure all order placement methods accept and propagate strategy_name
Implement Discord notifications in both Python fallback and Rust hot paths

jwt_token_expiration.problem: JWT tokens expire causing 500 errors on API calls, especially /api/Order/place
symptoms: 500 Internal Server Error on order placement
Max retries exceeded with url: /api/Order/place
ResponseError('too many 500 error responses')
Orders fail to place even when credentials are valid
root_causes: Token expires after ~30 minutes but code doesn't auto-refresh
Using expired token in Authorization header
No retry logic with token refresh on 500 errors
Calling authenticate() directly instead of _ensure_valid_token()

solutions.fix: Add automatic token refresh and retry on 500 errors
solutions.code_pattern: if 'error' in response and '500' in str(response.get('error', '')): await self._ensure_valid_token(); await asyncio.sleep(0.75); retry request

solutions.fix: Remove None values from JSON payloads (TopStepX rejects None)
solutions.code_pattern: cleaned_data = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if v is not None}

solutions.fix: Use _ensure_valid_token() instead of authenticate() on startup

prevention: Always use _ensure_valid_token() instead of authenticate() directly
Check token expiration before making API calls
Implement retry logic with token refresh on 500 errors
Add 0.75s delay before retry to prevent rate limiting
Log JSON payloads for debugging order placement issues

async_await_syntax_errors.problem: Using await in synchronous functions causes SyntaxError
symptoms: SyntaxError: 'await' outside async function
Line numbers pointing to await statements in sync methods
root_causes: Adding await to synchronous methods like _make_curl_request()
Forgetting to make function async when adding await
Mixing sync and async code incorrectly

solutions.pattern: If method is sync, handle async operations in caller
solutions.example: _make_curl_request() is sync, token refresh happens in async caller

solutions.pattern: Make function async if it needs await

prevention: Check function signature before adding await
If function is 'def', it's sync - handle async in caller
If function is 'async def', it can use await
Clear Python cache files if syntax errors persist: find . -name '*.pyc' -delete

account_tracker_missing_methods.problem: AccountTracker missing get_daily_pnl() method causing strategy failures
symptoms: 'AccountTracker' object has no attribute 'get_daily_pnl'
Strategies fail to analyze: Error analyzing MNQ/MES
No trade signals generated
root_causes: Strategy code calls tracker.get_daily_pnl() but method doesn't exist
Missing properties: current_balance, daily_loss_limit, etc.

solutions.fix: Add get_daily_pnl() method and required properties

prevention: Ensure AccountTracker implements all methods used by strategies
Check strategy_base.py for required tracker methods
Add properties for commonly accessed state values

signalr_connection_spam.problem: SignalR connection spam causing thousands of failed connection attempts
symptoms: Massive log spam (30,000+ logs/minute)
Continuous 403 Forbidden errors
Railway rate limit hit (500 logs/sec)
High CPU usage from failed reconnections
root_causes: reconnect_interval: 1 (retry every 1 second)
max_attempts: 0 (unlimited retries)
No exponential backoff
No special handling for 403 errors

solutions.fix: Implement exponential backoff and limit retries
Add 403 error detection to reduce log spam

prevention: Always set max_attempts for reconnection logic
Use exponential backoff for retries
Detect and handle specific error codes (403, 401) specially
Don't log the same error repeatedly

signalr_401_authentication_error.problem: SignalR WebSocket connections failing with 401 Unauthorized errors
symptoms: WebSocketBadStatusException: Handshake status 401 Unauthorized
SignalR Market Hub disconnected immediately after connection attempt
Connection timeout after 10 seconds
Real-time market data not available
root_causes: Token expired when SignalR tries to connect
Token not refreshed before connection attempt
access_token_factory using stale token (captured at connection time)
No token refresh on 401 errors

solutions.fix: Ensure token is valid before connecting - call ensure_valid_token() first
Use fresh token factory that always gets latest token
Handle 401 errors by refreshing token and reconnecting
New method to refresh token, stop connection, wait, and reconnect
solutions.details: Stops current hub, refreshes token, waits 1s, then calls start() again

prevention: Always call ensure_valid_token() before getting token for SignalR
Use token factory function instead of capturing token value
Handle 401 errors with automatic token refresh and reconnection
Don't suppress 401 errors - fix the root cause (expired token)
Test SignalR connection with token that's about to expire

strategy_status_keyerror.problem: strategies status command fails with KeyError: 'status'
symptoms: KeyError: 'status' when running 'strategies status'
Strategy status display fails
root_causes: OvernightRangeStrategy.get_status() overrides base method without calling super()
Missing required fields from base class

solutions.fix: Call super().get_status() first, then add custom fields

prevention: Always call super() when overriding methods
Include all required fields from base class
Test CLI commands after strategy changes

excessive_api_calls.problem: Frontend polling too frequently causing slow dashboard
symptoms: Dashboard slow to load
Multiple API calls for same data
Slow API warnings (5+ seconds)
High API usage
root_causes: Overlapping polling calls (async fetches stack up when endpoints are slow)
Order/position endpoints performing expensive per-position linked-order lookups on every poll
Multiple tabs polling simultaneously

fixes: Make expensive linked-order enrichment opt-in (include_linked=1) instead of default
Add short TTL caching + a request lock to /api/chart/orders to prevent refresh storms
Use balances from list_accounts() instead of individual calls
Add React Query staleTime for better caching

prevention: Use appropriate polling intervals (not too frequent)
Leverage React Query caching
Use WebSocket for real-time updates when possible
Cache API responses on backend
Guard against overlapping refreshes (in-progress locks on frontend)

chart_realtime_updates.problem: Chart bars not updating in real-time
symptoms: Only 2m timeframe shows recent data
Other timeframes lag 20-30 minutes
Bars generated once and never updated
root_causes: Bar aggregator only supports limited timeframes
Frontend too strict about timeframe matching
Bar aggregator not initializing all requested timeframes

solutions.fix: Expand default timeframes to include all chart timeframes

fixes: Relax timeframe matching in WebSocket updates

prevention: Initialize all timeframes when symbol is registered
Don't be too strict about timeframe matching
Subscribe to timeframe-specific updates

excessive_logging_verbosity.problem: Terminal output is too verbose with INFO-level logs cluttering the console
symptoms: Terminal flooded with 'Fetching historical data' messages
INFO logs appearing in console during normal operation
Difficult to see important warnings/errors
User wants cleaner terminal output
root_causes: Both file and console handlers set to same log level (INFO)
No separation between file logging and console output
All INFO logs go to both file and console

solutions.fix: Set console_handler to WARNING level, keep file_handler at INFO level
solutions.code_pattern:
console_handler.setLevel(logging.WARNING)  # Only WARNING+ in terminal
file_handler.setLevel(getattr(logging, log_level, logging.INFO))  # All logs to file

solutions.fix: Add startup message indicating logs go to file
solutions.code_pattern:
print('ℹ️  Detailed logs are being written to: trading_bot.log')
print('   (Terminal will only show warnings and errors)')

prevention: Always separate file and console log levels
File handler should capture all logs (INFO+)
Console handler should only show important messages (WARNING+)
Add startup message to inform users where logs are written
Keep verbose flag to enable full console logging when needed

datetime_utcnow_deprecation.code_pattern:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
# Replace:
datetime.utcnow()
# With:
datetime.now(timezone.utc)
datetime_utcnow_deprecation.prevention: Always use timezone-aware datetime objects. Import timezone from datetime module.

datetime_timezone_mismatch.error: TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes
symptoms: Error when subtracting two datetime objects
One datetime is timezone-aware, the other is timezone-naive
root_causes: datetime.combine() creates timezone-naive datetime by default
Mixing datetime.now(timezone.utc) with datetime.combine() without tzinfo
Using datetime.utcnow() (naive) with datetime.now(timezone.utc) (aware)
datetime_timezone_mismatch.fix: Ensure both datetimes are timezone-aware when performing arithmetic
datetime_timezone_mismatch.code_pattern:
# Wrong:
now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)  # aware
midnight = datetime.combine(date, time.min)  # naive
result = midnight - now  # ERROR!

# Correct:
now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)  # aware
midnight = datetime.combine(date, time.min, tzinfo=timezone.utc)  # aware
result = midnight - now  # OK!
prevention: Always specify tzinfo when using datetime.combine()
Use datetime.now(timezone.utc) instead of datetime.utcnow()
Ensure all datetime objects in arithmetic operations have the same timezone awareness
Use timezone.utc for UTC operations

recent_fixes.issue: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'query' in WebSocket broadcast loop

Use conditional expressions: request.query.get('key') if request else None

This properly handles async operations from synchronous SignalR callbacks without warnings.

recent_fixes.issue: Real-time chart showing time gaps, incorrect volume, and positions API 500 errors
recent_fixes.fix: ✅ FIXED! Three issues resolved: (1) **Time gaps**: Changed timestamp calculation from `int(current_time.timestamp())` to `int(current_time.timestamp() // 60 * 60)` to round down to minute boundary, preventing sub-minute timing differences from creating gaps. (2) **Volume**: Changed from using total daily volume to calculating volume delta between updates. Track last known volume in cache and add delta to current bar. Initialize new bars with volume delta from last bar. (3) **Positions 500 error**: Changed status from 500 to 200 with empty array when positions fetch fails, added detailed logging. This keeps chart functional even if positions endpoint has issues.

lessons_learned: For bar aggregation, always round timestamps to bar boundary (e.g., minute boundary for 1m bars) to prevent gaps
Volume from quotes is total daily volume, not bar volume - must calculate delta between updates
API endpoints should return 200 with empty data instead of 500 errors when possible to keep UI functional
Cache both bar data and last known volume for accurate delta calculations
Use `timestamp // 60 * 60` to round down to minute boundary (or `// period * period` for other periods)

recent_fixes.issue: Chart not showing current bars during Sunday evening session - showing stale Friday data instead of live Sunday 6pm+ data

(2) **CRITICAL**: Fixed _get_last_market_close() to correctly handle Sunday evening session. Original code checked `weekday == 6` (Sunday) but at 00:55 Monday morning EST, weekday is 0 (Monday), yet it's still the Sunday evening trading session (which runs Sunday 6pm - Monday 5pm EST). New logic: Market is open if (Sunday 6pm+) OR (Monday before 5pm) OR (Tue-Thu except 5-6pm) OR (Friday before 5pm). Returns current time when market is open, last close when market is closed.
recent_fixes.impact: Charts now correctly show live data during Sunday evening sessions and all trading hours. Critical fix for 24/5 futures market hours.
lessons_learned: Futures markets trade Sunday 6pm - Friday 5pm EST (24/5 with daily breaks)
Sunday evening session continues into Monday morning (until Monday 5pm EST)
Python weekday(): 0=Monday, 6=Sunday. At 00:55 Monday EST, it's still Sunday evening session
Don't just check weekday - check both weekday AND hour to determine if market is open
Market hours logic must account for sessions that span midnight (Sunday 6pm → Monday 5pm)
Always return current time when market is open, not a past close time

recent_fixes.issue: Chart x-axis times 5 hours ahead of actual time - timezone issue causing price bar discrepancies
recent_fixes.fix: ✅ FIXED! When converting Bar objects to dictionaries for chart display, the code used `bar.timestamp.isoformat()` to create a string. Problem: If bar.timestamp is timezone-naive (no tzinfo), isoformat() produces a string without timezone info (e.g., '2025-12-08T05:00:00'). When parsed back with fromisoformat(), it creates a naive datetime, and .timestamp() treats it as local time (EST) instead of UTC, adding 5 hours. Solution: Convert timestamps directly to Unix seconds when creating dict, checking if naive and assuming UTC if so: `int(bar.timestamp.replace(tzinfo=tz.utc).timestamp()) if bar.timestamp.tzinfo is None else int(bar.timestamp.timestamp())`. This skips string serialization entirely.
recent_fixes.impact: Chart now displays correct times in UTC. Bars align properly without timezone-induced price discrepancies.
lessons_learned: Never serialize datetime to ISO string and back when working with timestamps - convert directly to Unix seconds
If datetime is naive (no tzinfo), calling .timestamp() assumes local timezone, not UTC
Always check if datetime.tzinfo is None before calling .timestamp() - add UTC if naive
For charts expecting Unix timestamps, convert directly: int(dt.timestamp()), don't use isoformat()
Timezone-naive datetimes are dangerous - they're interpreted as local time, causing 5-hour shifts (EST offset)

recent_fixes.issue: PyO3 0.20 parameter passing bug - async methods don't expose all parameters to Python
recent_fixes.fix: ⚠️ WORKAROUND APPLIED - Disabled Rust cancel_order implementation, using Python fallback. Root cause: PyO3 0.20 with abi3-py38 has known issue where additional parameters in async methods aren't properly exposed to Python bindings. Tried: (1) #[pyo3(signature = (order_id, account_id))] - ignored. (2) #[pyo3(text_signature = ...)] - ignored. (3) Keyword-only args with * - ignored. (4) State-based approach with set_account_id() - method not exported. Actual fix requires upgrading to PyO3 0.21+.
recent_fixes.impact: Python fallback works (43-47ms execution time). Re-enable Rust after upgrading PyO3.
lessons_learned: PyO3 0.20 has parameter exposure bugs in async methods - use 0.21+ for production
inspect.signature() in Python shows what parameters are actually exposed
Rust code can be correct but Python binding may not expose all parameters
Always test Python bindings with actual calls, not just compilation
State-based workarounds (set_account_id) also fail if methods not exported to Python

simulation_daily_atr_wrong.problem: Daily ATR calculation in simulation returns wrong value (7.25 instead of 269.04)
symptoms: Daily ATR shows same value as current timeframe ATR (e.g., 7.25)
ATR zones are too small and inside the overnight range
Log shows 'calculated from 200 daily bars: 7.25' instead of correct value
root_causes: Strategy replay engine mocked trading_bot.get_historical_data to always return the in-memory replay bars list, ignoring requested timeframe (e.g., '1d' or '5m')
As a result, daily ATR was computed from partial intraday replay bars (small TR), making 'daily' ATR collapse to ~the intraday ATR
Secondary: when using real daily bars, you must still exclude the current incomplete daily bar from ATR inputs

solutions.fix: Filter out incomplete daily bars by comparing bar date with current date. Only use complete daily bars (from previous days) for ATR calculation.

Use current bar timestamp from replay engine instead of fetching bars

session_replay_simple.problem: Full StrategyReplayEngine bar-by-bar replay can distort strategy context (overnight range / market open / ATR) or add complexity when you only want session playback + order-event recording
session_replay_simple.goal: Use analyze_date as the single source of truth for the day's setup, then replay only the regular session (08:00–16:00 ET) bars and record order events without live execution pathways

details: Call analyze_date first to get correct overnight range + daily ATR zones for the date

Seed OvernightRangeStrategy caches and override calculate_atr/track_overnight_range to return the analyze_date-derived context
Iterate bars oldest->newest and record entry/exit events when price crosses bracket levels (simple OCO + conservative same-bar handling)
